newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Court repeals fugitive banker claim.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Court repeals fugitive banker claim.

text.p: Venezuela's Supreme Court has overturned fugitive banker Alvaro Stelling's claim to recover his shares in Bancos de Venezuela and Consolidado, the Court said.
"The Court has found Stelling's demand against Fogade as inadmissible," said the Court in a statement.
In a separate release Fogade, which owns over 99 percent of each of the bank's shares, said the Court's finding opened the way for the banks' public auction of the banks.
"All possible legal obstacles have been removed... now there can exist no doubt that Fogade is the legitimate owner of its shares in these banks."

Stelling's suit alleged he was coerced into selling his shares in the two banks for a symbolic bolivar when they collapsed during the country's 1994-5 financial crisis. In essence, Stelling argued the banks were still his.

The claim muddied Banco de Venezuela's slated August auction -- which was to flagship Venezuela's privatisation drive -- which was called-off only two days before the sale after a judge alleged there had been irregularities in the process.
Banco de Venezuela's sale was subsequently re-scheduled for the end of the year.
